title: Timeout dispatch after the first hit
statement: Let $H$ be a $k$-tape Turing machine with state set $Q$, let $S$ be a finite type, and let $\tau : \mathrm{Option}(S) \to Q$ be a timeout-state map. If the run of $H$ from a configuration $a$ is in state $\tau(r)$ after $t$ steps for some $r$, and no run at any earlier time $u<t$ is in any state $\tau(r')$, then the timeout runner, started from $a$ with its state tagged as the running phase, is after $t+1$ steps exactly the configuration reached by $H$ after $t$ steps, with its state replaced by the halted runner phase.
